old: Thorn forests occur in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Rayalaseema, in the 25–75 cm rainfall range.
new: Tropical thorn forests grow where rainfall is below 70 cm, in Rajasthan, Kutch, Saurashtra and western Andhra Pradesh, that is, Rayalaseema.

old: Chhattisgarh had the third-largest forest cover, measuring about 55,812 sq km. Odisha had about 61,204 sq km, while Meghalaya was notable for the share of its geographical area under forest.
new: By forest area, Madhya Pradesh (77,073 sq km) is first, Arunachal Pradesh (65,882 sq km) second and Chhattisgarh (55,812 sq km) third.

old: The stated counts are 109 National Parks and 573 Wildlife Sanctuaries. The figure 688 refers to the combined number of National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries in another cited count.
new: India has 109 National Parks and 573 Wildlife Sanctuaries (2026 counts); 127 is the number of Conservation Reserves.

old: Option C is incorrect: dense forests cluster near the equator, where heat and rain are greatest. Bhutan's 70% forest rule, poor rainforest soil and Canada's softwood lead are right.
new: Option C is incorrect: dense forests gather near the equator. Bhutan's Constitution keeps at least 60% of its area under forest, rainforest soil is nutrient-poor and regrows slowly after clearing, and Canada is the largest producer and exporter of softwood timber and wood pulp.

old: Kalimantan is the Indonesian part of Borneo; Borneo itself is shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei and covers about 743,000 km².
new: Kalimantan is the Indonesian part (about 73%) of Borneo. Borneo itself, about 7.5 lakh sq km and the largest island of Asia, is shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.

old: Nanda Devi belongs to the Greater Himalaya (Himadri), not the Middle Himalaya as some notes wrongly place it.
new: Nanda Devi (7,817 m), in the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand, is a peak of the Greater Himalaya (Himadri), not the Middle Himalaya.

old: Minicoy is the largest and southernmost island; the Amindivi group lies north of 11° N.
new: Minicoy is the southernmost island of Lakshadweep and its second largest; the largest is Andrott. The Amindivi group lies north of 11° N.

old: The Gandak enters India at Valmikinagar, not Raxaul. Ramganga joins near Farrukhabad, Yamuna at Prayagraj and Son near Maner.
new: The Gandak enters India at Valmikinagar, not Raxaul, so this pair is wrong. The other pairs are right: the Son joins the Ganga near Maner, the Yamuna at Prayagraj and the Ramganga near Kannauj.

old: The order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (about 1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (858 km) and Tapi (724 km).
new: The order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (about 1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (851 km) and Tapi (724 km).

old: Chronically drought-prone areas get under 750 mm of rain and cover about 33% of India; drought-prone areas get 750–1125 mm and cover about 35%.
new: Chronically drought-prone areas get less than 750 mm of rain and make up about 33% of India's agricultural land; drought-prone areas get 750–1,125 mm and make up about 35%.

old: The Eastern Ghats peak in the Chintapalli–Paderu area of Alluri Sitharama Raju district, home to Jindhagada (1690 m). Dolphin's Nose is only 335 m.
new: The maximum height of the Eastern Ghats in AP is in the Chintapalli (Paderu) area of ASR district, where Arma Konda (1,680 m), the highest peak, stands. Dolphin's Nose is only 335 m.

old: The Nagavali rises in Odisha's Rayagada hills and enters AP in Srikakulam district.
new: The Nagavali (Langulya) rises in the Rayagada (Rayagarh) hills of Odisha, flows through Vizianagaram and Srikakulam and meets the sea at Mopasu Bandar.

old: The child sex ratio was 927 in 2001 and about 918–919 in 2011 (914 provisional).
new: The child sex ratio was 927 in 2001 and fell to 918 in 2011 (914 provisional).

old: The Bill, passed in August 2026, sought uniform rates by restricting States' power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land. It was criticised on grounds of fiscal federalism.
new: The 2026 Bill (August) sought to limit States' power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land. This raised a fiscal federalism debate.

old: Option 3 describes Caucasoid traits; Mongoloids have straight black hair and epicanthic folds.
new: Option 1 is the incorrect description: wavy hair and a narrow nose are Caucasoid traits, while Mongoloids have straight hair, oblique eyes with an epicanthic fold and a flat face. The Caucasoid and Negroid (woolly hair, broad nose) descriptions are correct.

old: Sindhi was added in 1967 (21st Amendment); the Telugu Language Act was 1966, Tamil became the first classical language in 2004 and Telugu in 2008.
new: Sindhi was added in 1967 by the 21st Amendment, the first addition to the Eighth Schedule, raising the total from 14 to 15.

old: The 96th Amendment (2011) only renamed 'Oriya' as Odia; it added no language.
new: Statement 1 is correct: the Eighth Schedule began with 14 languages in 1950. Statement 3 is correct: Sindhi was the first addition, by the 21st Amendment in 1967. Statement 2 is wrong: the 96th Amendment (2011) only renamed 'Oriya' as Odia and added no new language.

old: The 2024 revision dropped 'original, not borrowed'; knowledge texts and epigraphic evidence were added. (Sequence not possible: the facts carry no order.)
new: The 2024 revision dropped the 'original, not borrowed' requirement and added knowledge texts and epigraphic evidence as criteria.

old: These projects clash with tribal protections in the 1/70 Regulation, PESA and the Forest Rights Act. (Match not possible honestly from the facts; written as a one-liner.)
new: Pumped storage, bauxite and Polavaram projects clash with the tribal protections of the 1/70 Regulation, PESA and the Forest Rights Act.

old: AP's rural population was 349.47 lakh, about 70.5%; the urban share was about 29.5%.
new: AP's rural population was 349.67 lakh, about 70.5%; the urban share was about 29.5%.

old: In 1953, Bellary taluk was divided linguistically: Telugu-speaking areas went to Andhra and Kannada-speaking areas went to Mysore.
new: In 1953 Bellary district was divided by language: the Telugu areas went to Andhra and the Kannada areas to Mysore.

old: Tube wells lead with 47.3 per cent of net irrigated area; canals have 24.7 and tanks only 2.8 per cent (canals lead only in AP).
new: Tube wells lead with 49.34 per cent of India's net irrigated area (2022-23); canals have 22.85 per cent and tanks only 2.82 per cent. Canals lead only in AP.

old: The policy dates from 2008; 24 airports got in-principle approval and 13, including Navi Mumbai, are operational.
new: The Greenfield Airports Policy dates from 2008. Under it, 13 greenfield airports, including Navi Mumbai, are operational.

old: Portland Pozzolana Cement uses fly ash from thermal power plants and slag from steel plants.
new: Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) uses fly ash from thermal power plants, and Portland Slag Cement (PSC) uses slag from steel plants. So the pair is fly ash and slag.

old: UP, Maharashtra and Karnataka lead in sugar; cement leads in AP, Rajasthan, MP and Karnataka; fertiliser at Sindri and the Chota Nagpur steel towns.
new: Uttar Pradesh (35%), Maharashtra (22%) and Karnataka (10%) have the largest long-run shares of sugar output. Cement is led by Rajasthan and AP, and Gujarat is the largest fertiliser producer.

old: INDAL is associated with Muri, Alupuram and Belur. Jharsuguda is the location of India's largest aluminium smelter, operated by Vedanta.
new: INDAL is linked with Muri, Alupuram and Belagavi, not Jharsuguda. Jharsuguda has India's largest aluminium smelter, run by Vedanta. BALCO–Korba, NALCO–Damanjodi and HINDALCO–Renukoot are correct.

old: Software Technology Parks of India were set up in 1991. STPs along with EMC 2.0 support the IT and software sector.
new: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) were set up in 1991. Major IT clusters are Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai and Noida.

old: The APSES and CDI references identify the Asian Development Bank (ADB) as the VCIC partner; JICA is mentioned only in a conflicting January 2026 note.
new: VCIC is partly funded by an Asian Development Bank (ADB) loan, not JICA. ADB gives US$625 million of the US$840 million programme.

old: The four PCPIRs are Visakhapatnam-Kakinada, Dahej, Paradip and Cuddalore-Nagapattinam; Visakhapatnam-Kakinada is the Andhra Pradesh one. (Sequence not possible: no dates given.)
new: The four PCPIRs are Visakhapatnam-Kakinada, Dahej, Paradip and Cuddalore-Nagapattinam. Visakhapatnam-Kakinada is the one in Andhra Pradesh.

old: In the ODOP list, West Godavari's products are Narsapur crochet laces and processed prawn and shrimp.
new: In the ODOP list, Narsapur crochet laces are the product of West Godavari district. Uppada Jamdani sarees are Kakinada's and Machilipatnam Kalamkari is Krishna's.

old: PLFS 2025 gave AP 71.40%, down from 72.60% in 2023-24; the 82.10% claim has no official estimate.
new: PLFS 2025 (published 2 July 2026) put AP's literacy at 71.40%, down from 72.60% in 2023-24 and up from 69.1% in 2018-19.

old: The Jaunsari practise agriculture and polyandry; the Raji practised jhum, the Gond hunt and fish, and the Gaddi herd livestock.
new: The Jaunsari of Jaunsar-Bawar (Dehradun, Uttarakhand) are known for polyandry along with settled farming. The Gaddi are transhumant shepherds, not a polyandrous farming tribe.

old: Srikakulam (Garbham area) leads AP in manganese production and reserves. Kurnool leads in limestone and Kadapa in asbestos.
new: Vizianagaram (Garbham) is first in Andhra Pradesh in manganese production and reserves. Kurnool is first in limestone and Kadapa in asbestos.

old: Asbestos occurs in the Cuddapah system of Kadapa, at Pulivendula.
new: Kadapa stands first in asbestos in Andhra Pradesh; it occurs in the Cuddapah system there, at Pulivendula.

old: Thornthwaite's moisture order runs perhumid or wet, humid, semi-arid and arid, so arid is the driest type.
new: Thornthwaite's moisture order runs perhumid (A), humid (B), sub-humid (C), semi-arid (D) and arid (E), so arid is the driest type.

old: The 8 billion mark was reached on 15 November 2022 (UPSC). 11 July is World Population Day, 2011 is the 7 billion year, and 2024 is after the milestone.
new: World population reached 8 billion on 15 November 2022. 11 July is World Population Day, 2011 was the 7 billion year, and 2024 is after the milestone.

old: ITDC (India Tourism Development Corporation) was set up in 1966. The others are mismatched: 2002 is the year of the Incredible India campaign, Paryatan Didi was launched on 27 September 2024, and 1966 belongs to ITDC, not the Tourist Facilitator certification; Travel for LiFE is listed among the recent (2026) tourism initiatives, not a 2014 launch.
new: ITDC was set up in 1966. Paryatan Didi was launched on 27 September 2024 (2002 is the year of the Incredible India campaign), 1966 belongs to ITDC and not to the Tourist Facilitator certification, and Travel for LiFE is a sustainable, responsible tourism initiative, not a 2014 launch.

old: Kalinjar Hill is located in Banda district of Uttar Pradesh, not Nandyal. Belum Caves are located in Nandyal, Andhra Pradesh; Erra Matti Dibbalu are near Bheemunipatnam; and Akal Wood Fossil Park is in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan.
new: Kalinjar Hill is in Banda district of Uttar Pradesh, not Nandyal (Nandyal has Belum Caves). Erra Matti Dibbalu are at Bheemunipatnam, Akal Wood Fossil Park is in Jaisalmer and the Buxa Formation stromatolites are in Sikkim.

old: Mypadu is associated with Nellore district, not Machilipatnam. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
new: Mypadu beach is in SPSR Nellore district, not near Machilipatnam. Uppada is in Kakinada district, Yarada in Visakhapatnam and Suryalanka near Bapatla.

old: Maredumilli is in Polavaram district, not Nandyal district. Araku, Lambasingi and Papikondalu are correctly matched with their stated features.
new: Maredumilli is in Polavaram district, not Nandyal district. Papikondalu is in the Godavari gorge, Araku Valley is in Alluri Sitharama Raju district and Lambasingi is called the Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh.

old: Anthracite has 80–95% carbon; bituminous has 40–80%, lignite about 40–50% and peat less than 40%.
new: Anthracite has the highest carbon content, 80-95%. Bituminous coal has 40-80%, lignite 40-55% and peat less than 40%.

old: Lignite, or brown coal, contains approximately 40–50% carbon. Peat is the first stage of wood turning into coal, while anthracite is the highest grade.
new: Lignite is brown coal with high moisture and about 40-55% carbon. Peat (less than 40%) is the first stage of wood turning into coal, and anthracite (80-95%) is the highest grade.

old: Commercial production began at Digboi in 1889; the first well was drilled in 1866-67 and the refinery came in 1901.
new: Commercial oil production began at Digboi in 1889. The first oil well was drilled at Makum on 26 March 1867, and the Digboi refinery came in 1901.

old: Srisailam Right Bank Power House is 770 MW. 700 MW is the Sileru total, 1,760 MW Narla Tata Rao and 1,050 MW Rayalaseema TPS.
new: Srisailam Right Bank Power House is 770 MW. 700 MW is Upper and Lower Sileru combined, 1,050 MW is Rayalaseema TPS, and 1,760 MW is only the older part of Dr Narla Tata Rao TPS (now 2,560 MW).

old: Raniganj was associated with the first coal mine in 1774, Digboi with the first oil discovery in 1889, Tarapur with the first nuclear plant in 1969, and Pinnapuram is the later integrated renewable-energy storage project.
new: The first coal mine at Raniganj dates from 1774, Digboi's first commercial oil find from 1889 and Tarapur nuclear plant from 1969; Pinnapuram is the latest of the four.

old: NM-ICPS was approved by the Cabinet in 2018 with Rs 3,660 crore (for nine years per current sources; older sources say five), and set up 25 Technology Innovation Hubs. Rs 6,003.65 crore (2023) is the National Quantum Mission, Rs 10,371.92 crore (2024) is the IndiaAI Mission, and 2015 is the year NSM began.
new: NM-ICPS was approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 December 2018 with Rs 3,660 crore for five years and sets up 25 Technology Innovation Hubs. Rs 6,003.65 crore (2023) is the National Quantum Mission and Rs 10,371.92 crore (2024) is the IndiaAI Mission.

old: SSI Mantra is India's first indigenous surgical robotic system; Manav is India's first 3D-printed humanoid (2017).
new: SSI Mantra, developed by SS Innovations (Dr Sudhir Srivastava), is India's first indigenous surgical robotic system. Manav is India's first 3D-printed humanoid (built in late 2014), not a surgical robot.

old: UPI accounted for 49% of the world's real-time payments and recorded a FY 2025–26 high.
new: UPI handles about 49% of the world's real-time payments. In FY 2025-26 it also made up about 85% of India's digital payments by volume.

old: Measures for responding to deepfakes include the ECI advisory on mandatory labels for AI content in campaigns, DPDP Act penalties and I4C takedowns.
new: The ECI advisory makes labels on AI-generated content in election campaigns mandatory; this is one of the listed responses to deepfakes. The DPDP Act gives penalties and the EU AI Act mandates watermarking.

old: AP Police signed an MoU with IIT Tirupati for the academy, focused on digital forensics and blockchain tracing.
new: AP Police signed an MoU with IIT Tirupati for a Cyber Crime Investigation and Training Academy.

old: Gobind recognised privacy as part of personal liberty. Kharak Singh is linked with early privacy concerns under Article 21, and Puttaswamy affirmed privacy as a Fundamental Right and informational privacy.
new: Gobind v State of MP (1975) treated privacy as part of personal liberty. Kharak Singh (1962) was overruled by Puttaswamy insofar as it denied privacy, so it did not recognise privacy as a Fundamental Right. Puttaswamy (2017) was not an early case: its nine judges unanimously held privacy a Fundamental Right under Article 21.

old: Protein can be burnt for energy and yields about 4 kcal per gram. (No dated facts for a sequence, so a one-liner.)
new: One gram of protein gives about 4 kcal of energy; fat gives about 9.3 kcal per gram.

old: Chandrayaan-3 launched on 14 July 2023, before Aditya-L1 (2 Sep 2023), XPoSat (1 Jan 2024) and SpaDeX (30 Dec 2024). (Sequence not targeted; one-liner as asked.)
new: Chandrayaan-3 was launched on 14 July 2023 on LVM3-M4 and soft-landed on 23 August 2023.

old: DRDO Young Scientist Laboratories comprise five laboratories, not fifteen. The figure of fifteen refers to the DIA-CoEs and, in another context, new DRDO centres.
new: DRDO Young Scientist Labs are 5 labs in 5 futuristic areas, not 15; 15 is the number of DIA-CoEs. JCBCAT is at Jadavpur University, Kolkata and DIAT Pune is a deemed university, so those pairs are correct.

old: Akash has about 25–30 km; Nag is 4–7 km, Trishul about 9 km, and Agni ranges from about 700 km to over 5,000 km.
new: Akash, a medium-range SAM, has a range of about 25–30 km. Trishul reaches about 9 km, Nag 500 m to 4 km (land version), and Agni about 700 km to over 5,000 km.

old: Agni-II (2,000–3,000 km) is two-stage solid-fuel; Agni-IV (about 4,000 km) is two-stage road-mobile, Agni-III is about 3,500 km, and three-stage canister launch is Agni-V.
new: Agni-II is a two-stage solid-fuel missile (2,000–3,500 km). Agni-IV is two-stage and road-mobile (about 4,000 km), Agni-III has about 3,500 km range, and the three-stage canisterised missile is Agni-V.

old: The Energy Transition Index is published by the World Economic Forum. The State Energy and Climate Index is associated with BEE, the National Generation Adequacy Plan with CEA, and India Energy Outlook with IEA.
new: The Energy Transition Index is published by the World Economic Forum. The State Energy and Climate Index is by NITI Aayog, the National Generation Adequacy Plan by CEA, and India Energy Outlook by the IEA.

old: CBM is partly free in joints and partly adsorbed in micropores; it is called sweet gas because it has few heavier hydrocarbons.
new: CBM lies free in the joints of coal seams and is adsorbed in the micropores of coal, so 'micropores – adsorbed form' is correct and the two joint/micropore pairs given the other way are wrong. CBM is called 'sweet gas'; it is not a gas rich in heavier hydrocarbons.

old: A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notice in a petition challenging the liability caps under SHANTI.
new: In August 2026 a Supreme Court Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant issued notice on a petition challenging the liability caps under the SHANTI Act, 2025.

old: L. J. Stadler first demonstrated mutation breeding using X-rays in 1930. Gamma and neutron radiation are also used subsequently for inducing mutations.
new: L. J. Stadler first induced mutation in crop plants in 1928, using X-rays on barley. Gamma and neutron radiation were used later for mutation breeding.

old: The revised 100 GW comprised 40 GW rooftop and 60 GW large/medium grid-connected projects. (Only one date is given, so a sequence could not be built.)
new: The revised target of June 2015 was 100 GW by 2022: 40 GW rooftop and 60 GW large/medium grid-connected projects.

old: Renewables rise from about 20% (2024-25) to about 80% by 2070, while coal falls from about 74% to 6-10%.
new: NITI Aayog's net-zero scenarios see renewables giving about 80% of power generation by 2070. Today coal, not renewables, gives over 74% of generation, and coal's share falls sharply by 2070.

old: Industry remains the largest sector, with 8,764 TWh under BAU in 2040, while cooking demand falls as clean fuels replace biomass.
new: Industry uses about half of India's electricity and stays the largest consumer by 2040, while cooking demand falls.

old: The current estimate identifies India as the world’s fifth-largest holder of coal reserves; an older estimate had placed it fourth.
new: India has the world's fifth-largest coal reserves, though it is the second-largest coal producer.

old: NIWE puts Andhra Pradesh's wind potential at about 74.90 GW at 120 m (about 123 GW at 150 m).
new: NIWE puts Andhra Pradesh's wind potential at about 74.90 GW at 120 m hub height. Gujarat is highest at 142.56 GW.

old: The amendment allowed new members to be added to the NBCC.
new: The 2022 amendment allowed new members to be added to the NBCC, so saying it barred them is wrong. It also allowed more feedstocks, biofuel production in SEZs/EOUs under Make in India, and export of biofuels in specific cases.

old: The Numaligarh plant uses bamboo, a non-food lignocellulosic (second-generation) feedstock.
new: Numaligarh (Golaghat, Assam) is India's first commercial bamboo bioethanol plant, dedicated on 14 September 2025. Panipat is the first commercial 2G plant; Bathinda and Bargarh are other 2G plants.

old: FAO FRA 2025 puts forests at about 32% of Earth's land. 54% is the share of forests held by five countries (Russia, Brazil, Canada, USA, China), and 21.76 (Mha) is the land India restored in 2011-2020.
new: FAO FRA 2025 puts forests at about 32% of Earth's land. 54% is the share of world forests held by five countries (Russia, Brazil, Canada, USA, China); 21.76% and 25.17% are India's forest cover and forest-plus-tree cover in ISFR 2023.

old: Dust storms in Rajasthan and north-west India are most common in the hot, dry pre-monsoon months, peaking in May.
new: Dust storms in Rajasthan and north-west India are most common in the hot, dry pre-monsoon summer months (April to June).

old: The NGT told the State to pay the compensation to the APPCB within three months.
new: On 2 December 2021 the NGT ordered the AP government to pay about Rs 243 crore environmental compensation to the APPCB for violations in the Polavaram, Pattiseema, Purushottapatnam and Chintalapudi projects.

old: The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified in 2010; a sequence could not be built honestly from these facts.
new: The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve in Andhra Pradesh was notified in 2010. It is home to Red Sanders, Cycas beddomei and the micro-endemic Golden Gecko.

old: Warmer air holds about 7% more moisture per 1°C, which intensifies extreme rainfall and flash floods. (No dates for a sequence, so a one-liner.)
new: Warmer air holds about 7% more moisture for each 1°C of warming, so rain events become more extreme and flash floods increase.

old: Heat stress is specifically noted in Rayalaseema. Coastal erosion is associated with Uppada, while the other two pairs assign unrelated risks or locations.
new: Heat is rising in Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur; Kurnool and Anantapur lie in Rayalaseema, so Rayalaseema–heat stress is the correct pair. Coastal erosion belongs to Uppada (Kakinada), not Palnadu, and the other two pairs give risks that do not fit those places.

old: About 68% of India is drought-prone, largely because of rain-fed agriculture.
new: About 68% of India is drought-prone (NDMA). The main cause is inadequate and uneven rainfall.

old: The rename to UNDRR came in 2019; 1989–1999 was the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.
new: UNISDR was renamed UNDRR on 1 May 2019; UNDRR is based in Geneva. The International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction ran from 1990 to 1999.

old: IS 1893 governs earthquake-resistant design, a structural earthquake-mitigation measure.
new: IS 1893 is the Indian Standard for earthquake-resistant design. Building codes like IS 1893 are non-structural mitigation measures for earthquakes.

old: 22 April is Earth Day; World Meteorological Day is the day declared by the World Meteorological Organization.
new: World Meteorological Day is observed on 23 March, not 22 April. 22 April is Earth Day, and 13 October is the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction.

old: India joined in 1982 and has 101 Ramsar sites, the most in Asia.
new: India became a Party to the Ramsar Convention in 1982. The Convention itself was signed on 2 February 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.

old: India reached 101 sites with Glaw Lake and 103 on 16 October 2026 with Sukhna Lake and Sauj Jheel.
new: On 16 October 2026 India's Ramsar tally reached 103, with the addition of Sukhna Lake (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh).

old: Project Elephant began in 1992. Project Tiger began in 1973, the NGT in 2010, and the NTCA is a statutory body.
new: Project Elephant began in 1992. Project Tiger began in 1973 (not 2010), the NGT was set up in 2010 (not 1992), and the NTCA was set up in 2006 (not 1973).

old: An ecotone is the transition zone where two ecosystems meet, such as forest and grassland. Lentic means still water, and a sere is a stage in succession.
new: An ecotone is the transition zone where two communities meet, such as a grassland between forest and desert. Lentic means still water, a sere is the whole sequence of communities in succession, and an anthrome is a human-altered biome.

old: The NAMASTE scheme aims to formalise informal workers, who handle more than 70% of recycled plastic.
new: NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem) aims to bring informal sanitation workers, and since 2024 waste pickers, into the formal system with safety and dignity. PM SVANidhi, PM-DAKSH and Stand-Up India are other schemes.

old: Operation Clean Sweep is the Municipal Administration Department’s campaign for scientific solid-waste management in Tier-1 and Tier-2 corporations.
new: Operation Clean Sweep (May–June 2026) is the Municipal Administration Department's sanitation drive for scientific solid-waste management in all 123 ULBs: clearing garbage black spots, cleaning roads and drains and promoting segregation.

old: MSCs were first isolated from bone marrow; they can form bone, cartilage and fat cells. (No dates are given, so a one-liner replaces the sequence shape.)
new: Mesenchymal stem cells were first found in bone marrow. They can form bone, cartilage and fat cells.

old: HTBt cotton combines glyphosate tolerance with the Bt trait; its approval in India is pending over weed-management and socio-economic concerns.
new: HTBt cotton combines the Bt trait with tolerance to the herbicide glyphosate. It is not approved in India, so growing it is illegal.

old: The NBA was set up at Chennai in 2003; no dated sequence could be built honestly, so a one-liner is used.
new: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), the national tier under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, was set up at Chennai in 2003.

old: Neem is the state tree of Andhra Pradesh; Red Sanders is not, despite appearing as such in one list.
new: Neem is the state tree of Andhra Pradesh, not Red Sanders.

old: In 1730, Amrita Devi Bishnoi and 363 other Bishnois died at Khejarli while protecting khejri trees from the men of the Jodhpur king.
new: In 1730 at Khejarli, Amrita Devi and 363 Bishnois died protecting khejri trees from the Jodhpur king's men.

old: APSES lists one biosphere reserve, Seshachalam, and one tiger reserve, Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam.
new: Seshachalam (2010) is Andhra Pradesh's first and only biosphere reserve. Nallamala is a hill range, Papikonda a national park and Coringa a wildlife sanctuary.

old: Coringa WLS in Kakinada, together with Krishna WLS, forms the Godavari-Krishna estuarine mangroves, described as India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem. ⚠ Sources differ: ISFR 2023 puts Gujarat second, so this ranking follows the AP sources. It is not an alpine, coral reef or desert ecosystem.
new: Coringa WLS in Kakinada, with Krishna WLS, forms the Godavari-Krishna estuarine mangroves, often called India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem after the Sundarbans. By State, Gujarat has the second-largest mangrove cover. It is not an alpine, coral reef or desert ecosystem.

old: Canada withdrew in 2011 (some sources say 2012); the USA never ratified the Protocol.
new: Canada announced its withdrawal on 12 December 2011, effective 15 December 2012; it was the first country to leave Kyoto. The USA never ratified the Protocol.

old: The APPSC-GS 2024 key links Saraswathi of Malluvalasa (AP natural-farming practitioner) with 'Sustaina India 2025'. ⚠ Sources differ: one guide links her to COP28 instead, so check the official key.
new: Saraswathi of Malluvalasa (Vizianagaram), known for natural farming and millet revival, was featured at Sustaina India 2025, a CEEW exhibition held in New Delhi in February 2025 (APPSC-GS 2024). She is not linked to a COP28 recognition.

old: The International Solar Alliance was established at COP21 in 2015 with France and India. CDRI was established in 2019 in New Delhi.
new: The International Solar Alliance was launched at COP21 (2015) by India and France and has its HQ at Gurugram. CDRI was launched by India at the UN Climate Action Summit in New York in 2019 and has its HQ in New Delhi.

old: India has hosted the summits since January 2023 to press developing-country finance and technology needs; they are not a CBAM mechanism. (No dated series for a sequence, so a one-liner.)
new: India has hosted the Voice of Global South Summits since January 2023 to press developing countries' needs for finance and technology; they are not a CBAM mechanism.

old: The 45 percent emissions-intensity reduction commitment and the 50 percent renewable-energy commitment entered the August 2022 NDC.
new: The August 2022 NDC took in two Panchamrit pledges: a 45% cut in emissions intensity of GDP (from 2005) and the 50% target, written as a 50% non-fossil share of installed capacity, both by 2030.

old: Net zero balances residual emissions with removals such as forests and carbon capture, so gross emissions need not reach zero. (No dates for a sequence, so a one-liner.)
new: Net zero means residual emissions are balanced by removals such as forests and carbon capture, so gross emissions need not reach zero.
